title: You read it once and brushed past it.
paragraphs: You read it once and brushed past it.
“Meaningless, meaningless… everything is meaningless.” — Ecclesiastes 1:2
And something in you resisted it.
Because deep down, you’ve spent your whole life trying to prove the opposite.

You wake up, chase something, build something, fix something, scroll something—anything that makes you feel like your life is adding up to more than dust. You tell yourself, “This matters. This counts. This is worth it.”
But there are quiet moments you can’t escape.

When the noise fades.
When the achievement doesn’t satisfy.
When the distraction stops working.
And a question slips through:
Why does this still feel empty?
God saw it.
You knew.
The writer of Ecclesiastes—Solomon, a man who had more wisdom, wealth, pleasure, and success than most people will ever touch—didn’t speak from ignorance. He tested everything life could offer.

Power.
Knowledge.
Pleasure.
Work.
Possessions.
And after exhausting it all, he didn’t say, “Try harder.”
He said, “It’s meaningless.”
That word doesn’t mean life has no value. It means everything “under the sun”—everything disconnected from God—is like vapor.
Here, then gone.

You can chase it, but you can’t hold it.
You can build it, but you can’t keep it.
You can love it, but it will eventually leave you—or you will leave it.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Ecclesiastes isn’t trying to depress you.
It’s trying to wake you up.
Because the real tragedy isn’t that life is short.
It’s that you can spend it chasing things that were never meant to satisfy your soul.

You thought success would do it.
You thought relationships would fix it.
You thought money would secure it.
You thought distractions would numb it.
But every time you reached the top of something, you found the same thing waiting there:
Emptiness.
Not because those things are evil…
…but because they were never designed to be your god.
“Yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring… What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes.” — James 4:14
Read that again.
A mist.
That’s what Ecclesiastes is confronting.
Not to strip you of hope—but to redirect it.
Because if everything under the sun is temporary…
Then the only thing that isn’t meaningless must come from beyond the sun.
That’s where Jesus steps in.
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.” — John 14:6
Not a better version of your current life.
A completely different foundation.
Jesus doesn’t offer you more temporary satisfaction—He offers you eternal purpose.

While everything else fades, He remains.
While everything else fails, He saves.
While everything else leaves you empty, He fills what nothing else can reach.
“The world and its desires pass away, but whoever does the will of God lives forever.” — 1 John 2:17
This is the lesson Ecclesiastes forces you to face:
You can spend your entire life gaining everything…
…and still lose your soul.
Or you can surrender your life to Christ…
…and gain what cannot be taken from you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
There are only two directions from here.
Keep chasing what you already know won’t last.
Or finally admit what your soul has been whispering all along.
This isn’t working.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been chasing things that can’t satisfy me.”
That honesty matters more than you think.
And if you know someone who is exhausted from pretending their life is full when it isn’t… send this to them.
Let it interrupt them the way truth interrupted you.
Follow this path if you’re ready to stop living on the surface and start understanding what actually matters before your time runs out.

It’s about eternity.
